stories.title: No 10 Forced to Clarify Burnham Not Siding with Manchester City Over Finance Scandal
stories.summary: Andy Burnham's comments defending Manchester City's process sparked a political row this week, with No 10 issuing a clarification that 'there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules'. Conservatives called the original remarks 'completely out of touch'.

stories.title: Burnham Announces National Care Service at Labour Conference
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham used his keynote Labour conference speech in Liverpool (Sep 29) to announce plans for a National Care Service — free at the point of use — to be introduced in the next parliament, as his signature social policy ambition.

stories.title: The People Shaping Burnham's Grand Plans for Britain
stories.summary: The Guardian profiles the key figures around Andy Burnham — including Chancellor John Healey, First Secretary Louise Haigh, and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh — as the new PM sets out his ambitious domestic agenda.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🏗️ Burnham Strips Back Procurement Rules: British Jobs at Heart of £90bn Contracts
stories.summary: The Burnham Government is replacing wide green/social procurement targets with a jobs-first approach, scrapping net zero requirements for public contracts to prioritise job creation and 'Buy British' objectives across the £90bn contracts landscape.

stories.title: 🤖 PM's Top AI Adviser Jade Leung to Leave Post
stories.summary: Jade Leung, Prime Minister Burnham's senior AI adviser, is set to leave her role, raising questions about continuity in the government's centralised AI policy unit which Burnham set up within his own office from day one.

stories.title: 🏢 Burnham Searches for UK Alternative to Palantir for NHS Contract
stories.summary: PM Andy Burnham is actively seeking a UK-built alternative to Palantir's £330m NHS data contract, reflecting his 'Buy British' AI stance. The move puts the government's sovereignty agenda in tension with existing NHS operational dependencies on the US analytics firm.

stories.title: 🤖 Minister Cites Need for 'Competitive Tension' in Government Cloud and Software
stories.summary: A government minister warned this week that there must be greater 'competitive tension' in how the government sources cloud services and software, signalling possible moves to reduce over-reliance on major US hyperscalers like Microsoft and AWS.

stories.title: 🤖 Government to Create Specialist Insourcing Unit
stories.summary: The Burnham government is establishing a new specialist insourcing unit to bring more government digital and technology capability in-house, reducing dependence on external contractors and consultants — a key plank of the 'Buy British' agenda.

stories.title: 🤖 New Information Commission Replaces the ICO
stories.summary: The Information Commissioner's Office has been replaced by the new Information Commission as of 1 October 2026, a structural reform that changes the UK's data protection regulatory architecture with implications for public sector data handling and AI procurement.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, Lords, PMQs, legislation

stories.title: Autumn Budget Confirmed for 28 October 2026
stories.summary: The government has confirmed the next Budget will take place on Wednesday 28 October 2026, the most significant fiscal event since Burnham took office in July. Key decisions on public spending, welfare and investment are expected.

stories.title: Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill 2026-27 Progressing Through Parliament
stories.summary: The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill continues its parliamentary journey, with an e-petition debate on sentence reductions for late guilty pleas scheduled for Westminster Hall on 19 October. The bill is one of the most significant pieces of social legislation in the Burnham parliament.

stories.title: Health Bill 2026-27 Advances: Single Patient Record Debate Scheduled
stories.summary: The Health Bill is making progress, with a debate on government oversight of underperforming NHS trusts scheduled for 14 October 2026. The bill includes provisions for a 'single patient record', a flagship digital health commitment.

stories.title: Burnham Pledges National Care Service — Free at Point of Use — at Labour Conference
stories.summary: At Labour's 2026 annual conference in Liverpool, PM Andy Burnham announced his intention to create a National Care Service in the next parliament, with free personal care for older people and no care charges from basic state pension. The speech received a prolonged standing ovation.

stories.title: Trade Unions and MPs Urge Burnham to Revisit Party Funding Rules
stories.summary: Labour donors, MPs and trade unions have called on Andy Burnham to revisit the party's internal funding rules, reflecting tensions between the unions and the new leadership over influence and access after the change in PM.

stories.title: Social Care Plans 'Admirable But Changes Must Come Quickly', Says Guardian
stories.summary: A Guardian analysis this weekend praised Burnham's National Care Service ambition as admirable, but warned that workers in the care sector need immediate relief and that the next-parliament timeline is too slow given current pressures.

stories.title: Tory Conference Opens in Birmingham: Badenoch Cements 'Classic Conservative' Image
stories.summary: The Conservative Party conference opened in Birmingham this weekend, with Kemi Badenoch declaring herself 'a classic old school Conservative'. She unveiled policies including scrapping the £100k childcare cliff edge and 'tough love' benefit rules for under-25s.

stories.title: Badenoch Rules Out Electoral Pact with Reform UK
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has definitively ruled out an electoral pact with Reform UK as the party meets for its annual conference, despite Reform overtaking the Tories in opinion polls and poaching MPs from the Conservative benches.

stories.title: Guardian: Tories 'Still Searching for a Purpose' as Conference Season Ends
stories.summary: The Guardian's editorial view after the party conferences suggests the Conservatives remain without a clear identity, squeezed between Reform UK on the right and Labour's popular majority mandate on the left. Badenoch has yet to define a distinctive alternative vision.

stories.title: Lib Dem MPs Criticise Davey Over Pension Triple Lock Response
stories.summary: Several Liberal Democrat MPs have publicly criticised party leader Ed Davey for his response to the pension triple lock debate, reflecting internal tensions over policy positioning as the party adjusts to opposition following Labour's election victory.

stories.title: Davey Promises £17bn Income Tax Cut if Lib Dems Elected
stories.summary: Ed Davey unveiled a flagship £17bn income tax cut proposal at the Lib Dem conference in Brighton, alongside a £2bn plan to cut fuel duty, as the party positions itself as a credible centrist alternative ahead of the next general election.

stories.title: Lib Dems Could 'Hold Balance of Power' at Next Election, Analysis Suggests
stories.summary: Despite Ed Davey's relatively low profile, political analysts note that the Liberal Democrats' position in 'blue wall' seats means they could hold the balance of power if Labour's majority is eroded at the next election, giving the party significant strategic leverage.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage, party news and announcements

stories.title: Reform Receives Record £72m in Donations from Crypto Billionaires — Farage Says 'Compliant with Law Today'
stories.summary: Reform UK announced £72m in donations over the weekend from crypto billionaires Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo (£36m each). Ministers plan to cap donations from British expats at £100k backdated to March 2026. Farage insists the donations are '100% compliant with the law today'.

stories.title: Farage Questioned by Parliamentary Standards Commissioner Over £5m Gift
stories.summary: Nigel Farage spent about half an hour being questioned by the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner over a £5m personal gift, adding to scrutiny of Reform UK's funding as the party's financial bonanza faces government caps on expat donations.

stories.title: Farage: Burnham's Brexit Debate Reopening is 'Biggest Boost of My Career'
stories.summary: Nigel Farage told a Reform rally in Doncaster that Andy Burnham's moves to reopen the Brexit debate — hinting at a closer relationship with the EU — represent the biggest political gift to him personally, as it re-energises Reform's core voter base.

stories.title: Swinney Sets Target for Scottish Independence Referendum by 2031
stories.summary: Scottish First Minister John Swinney announced the SNP's aim to hold an independence referendum by 2031, renewing calls following Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech. The FM also called for Scotland to receive £1bn from the UK's social care reforms.

stories.title: Burnham Rules Out Handing Scotland or Wales Powers to Hold Independence Referendum
stories.summary: PM Burnham firmly ruled out granting Scotland or Wales the legal powers to hold independence referendums, saying other UK nations must agree to any constitutional change. The decision drew sharp criticism from the SNP.

stories.title: Analysis: Brexit Debate Complicates SNP Independence Strategy
stories.summary: The Herald Scotland analyses how Burnham's EU engagement signals could reshape the Scottish independence debate in unexpected ways, with some commentators arguing a potential EU referendum could either energise or fragment the independence movement.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: Burnham's July 2026 Cabinet: Healey at Treasury, Haigh as First Secretary
stories.summary: The key Burnham cabinet appointments from July 2026 remain in place: John Healey as Chancellor, Louise Haigh as First Secretary and Cabinet Office Minister, Angela Rayner at Housing, Jonathan Reynolds at Business, Lucy Powell at Education, and Lisa Nandy at Digital.

stories.title: AI Centralised in PM's Office: Kanishka Narayan as First Cabinet-Level AI Minister
stories.summary: On taking office, Burnham appointed Kanishka Narayan as the UK's first Cabinet-level AI minister while dismantling DSIT and creating the new Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST). AI policy sits at the heart of No 10.

stories.title: GDS Launches CustomerFirst Unit to Drive Government Service Transformation
stories.summary: The Government Digital Service launched a new 'CustomerFirst' unit in late September 2026 aimed at driving public-facing digital service transformation, a key priority aligned with Burnham's mission to 'rewire' government delivery for citizens.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent election results, polls

stories.title: Tories Hold Off Reform UK to Win Council By-elections
stories.summary: Conservatives beat Reform UK in recent council by-elections, including in Charnwood Borough Council, providing a boost for Badenoch as she heads into the party conference. The results suggest the Tories retain a core local vote over Reform.

stories.title: Green Leader Polanski: No Need to Win Holborn & Pancras By-election to Keep Authority
stories.summary: Green Party leader Adrian Polanski said he does not need to win the forthcoming Holborn & Pancras by-election — described as a 50/50 contest — to maintain his authority as party leader, as the Greens seek to build momentum from their conference season.

stories.title: YouGov: Badenoch Approval at 32% Favourable vs 47% Unfavourable
stories.summary: The latest YouGov polling gives Kemi Badenoch a 32% favourable vs 47% unfavourable rating as she heads into the Conservative conference, with Reform UK continuing to outpace the Tories in national opinion polls.

stories.title: Lords Return from Conference Recess: New Technologies and Heritage Railways on Agenda
stories.summary: The House of Lords is due to return from conference recess for the week of 12 October 2026, with members set to discuss changes on new technologies, heritage railways, and other matters. The Budget on 28 October will be a key early agenda item.

stories.title: Financial Services and Markets Bill Begins Lords Journey
stories.summary: The Financial Services and Markets Bill has begun its passage through the House of Lords, a significant piece of legislation covering UK market regulation post-Brexit and the government's financial services reform agenda.

stories.title: Hereditary Peers Bill Passed in March 2026 — Lords Now Fully Appointed Chamber
stories.summary: The hereditary peers bill passed its final parliamentary stage in March 2026, completing the removal of hereditary peers from the House of Lords. The Lords is now a fully appointed chamber, a milestone constitutional change enacted under the Labour government.
